scope: Pyramid of the Sun, Teotihuacan, Mexico (today)
title: Pyramid of the Sun
blurb: The Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan, Mexico, as it stands today: the five reconstructed talud-tablero tiers (the fifth added in the 1905-1910 restoration), the bare summit where the lost temple stood, the later Adosada platform, the Avenue of the Dead frontage, and the sacred cave tunnel beneath the pyramid. Explore {parts} named components across {systems} systems.

systems.name: Talud tiers
systems.description: The sloping faces of the five stepped tiers, built of cut tepetate blocks and adobe and faced with tezontle slabs. The lime plaster and painted murals are entirely gone, and many original facing stones were removed in the 1905-1910 restoration.

systems.name: Tablero panels
systems.description: Vertical framed panels set against the taluds, the signature talud-tablero style of Teotihuacan, stripped of their plaster finish.

systems.name: Cornices
systems.description: Horizontal moldings crowning each tier face, as reconstructed in the early 20th century.

systems.name: Tier treads
systems.description: The flat walkways between the tiers, stripped of their plaster finish.

systems.name: Grand staircase
systems.description: The broad central staircase climbing the west face toward the Avenue of the Dead, flanked by alfarda balustrade walls. What visitors climb today partly reflects the 1905-1910 reconstruction.

systems.name: Summit platform
systems.description: The bare summit platform at 65 m. The temple that stood here was destroyed by deliberate and natural forces before archaeological study, and nothing of it survives.

systems.name: Adosada platform
systems.description: The four-level platform built over the original west facade centuries after the pyramid was completed, decorated with sculpted feline heads.

systems.name: Avenue of the Dead frontage
systems.description: The 45 m wide north-south avenue running along the west side of the pyramid, shown as a frontage segment with the forecourt plaza. The avenue and its facades were cleared and consolidated in the 1960-1965 INAH restoration.

systems.name: Surrounding plaza
systems.description: Low platforms ringing the pyramid, shown in outline.

systems.name: Sacred cave and tunnel
systems.description: The man-made tunnel and cloverleaf chamber six metres beneath the pyramid, whose entrance was found in 1971.

systems.name: Site
systems.description: The ground plane of the 500 m site frame.

The present flat top partly reflects the 1905-1910 restoration. Exact platform extent is schematic.

explanations.cave entrance pit: The seven-metre-deep pit at the foot of the main staircase where archaeologist Ernesto Taboada found the tunnel entrance in 1971, during work on a sound-and-light show.
explanations.cave tunnel: The man-made tunnel running from the entrance pit to beneath the centre of the pyramid, six metres down. Rene Millon studied the tunnel system in 1959 and found sealed tunnels with pottery and hearths. The tunnel route is schematic.
explanations.cave cloverleaf chamber: The cloverleaf (quatrefoil) chamber at the end of the tunnel, looted in antiquity. Once thought to be the natural lava tube of the mythical Chicomoztoc, it is now considered man-made, possibly a royal tomb. Chamber shape is schematic.
explanations.serpentine mask offering: A cache with a green serpentine mask, like the offerings found in the tunnel. Placement is schematic.
explanations.pottery offering cache: A cache of pottery vessels, like those Rene Millon's team found in the sealed tunnels. Placement is schematic.
explanations.site ground: The ground plane of the 500 m site frame: the pyramid, its forecourt, the Avenue of the Dead frontage and the surrounding plaza in outline.
